intro: Rocky Creek is a master planned community of rolling hills and 300 acres of open space off Hamilton Pool Road. CleanzATX cleans windows here with pure water systems and sends no one up a ladder for exterior glass.

sections.h2: What Rocky Creek homes are like
paragraphs: Rocky Creek covers a lot of ground, with more than 300 acres kept as open space and several hundred homes spread across rolling hills. Prices run roughly $600K to $1M, which puts many houses in the family sized range: three to five bedrooms, two story plans, attached garages and covered patios. There is a Rocky Creek HOA and no gate, so access is easy. The greenbelts and trail corridors mean many backyards face open land rather than another fence, and plenty of homes have large windows to take that in.
Because the community was built in phases, you will see a mix of builder ages and finishes from street to street.

sections.h2: What Rocky Creek windows deal with
paragraphs: Open space is lovely to look at and rough on glass. Grass and cedar pollen blow in from the greenbelt, and in cedar season, December through February, the film builds up quickly. Spider webs and insects gather around eaves and in window tracks, especially on homes that back to preserve land. Sprinklers on sloped lots can throw water across lower windows and leave hard water spots, particularly on west facing walls where the sun bakes them. Wind carries dust across the ridge lines too, and rain turns that dust into streaks.
Screens take a beating from all of it, so a screen cleaning with the windows saves a second trip.

No gate means we drive straight in. Hills mean ground can be uneven, so we survey the yard before setting up the water fed poles, which reach up to three stories from the ground. That keeps ladders off siding and stone on the exterior. Inside, we use drop cloths and hand squeegee every pane, and ladders with cotton covers for tall stairwell windows. Rocky Creek homes often pair window cleaning with a house soft wash, since siding and stucco gather green growth in shaded corners. Neighbors who book the same week help us group stops, which is how we keep lead time near two weeks.
A 2,600 square foot home is about $260 for exterior glass. Plan around two to two and a half hours outside and about an hour and fifteen minutes inside.

faq.q: My backyard faces open land. Do I need to clean windows more often?
faq.a: Often yes. Pollen and dust from open space build up faster. Many homes like this choose a Quarterly or Triannual plan, which brings 15% off, a free yearly screen cleaning and the 7 day rain guarantee.

faq.q: Is my price based on windows or house size?
faq.a: Either. Exterior windows are $10 each, or about $0.10 per square foot of home. We usually quote whichever the homeowner finds easier, and homes average about 10 windows per 1,000 square feet.

faq.q: Can you clean windows on a sloped yard?
faq.a: Yes. The water fed poles work from the ground, so a slope is rarely an issue. We check the footing before we set up and tell you if any window needs special handling.
Yes. House soft wash in Rocky Creek starts at $0.20 per square foot, $400 minimum. It uses low pressure and a 12V soft wash system that is safe for stucco and painted siding.
For Rocky Creek homes, screens are $5, full screens $10 and solar screens $15. Cleaning them removes pollen and webs that otherwise blow back onto the glass.
